explanation: Cultural Atlas describes Egyptian business meetings as often running longer than planned and beginning with coffee, tea, and personal conversation to build trust, so punctuality is appreciated but schedules are genuinely fluid. It is considered rude to try to rush a meeting, and it may take several visits to accomplish something that would be a single meeting elsewhere.
local_tip: Arrive on time yourself, confirm the meeting a day or two beforehand, and expect the agenda to move slower than planned.

also_check.note: Punctuality is strictly observed; even a short delay is seen as disrespectful.
Arriving late is seen as unprofessional and a sign of poor planning.
Some delay is tolerated socially, but punctuality is still appreciated for business meetings.
